animation_declarations.name: default
animation_declarations.reason: the steady wave height field, rendered as the run's one still.
animation_declarations.exempt_reason: ARTEMIS is the phase-resolving elliptic mild-slope (Berkhoff) solver: it solves a boundary-value problem for a single monochromatic sea state and returns ONE field, the steady agitation coefficient Kd. The run has no simulation clock at all, which is why its result carries ONE record - there is no time evolution to animate, and the single field IS the whole answer.

notes: UNDER-RESOLVED BY DESIGN. An 8 s swell in ten metres of water is about a 78 m wave, and 30 m node spacing resolves it on roughly two nodes - enough to prove the diffraction plumbing, not enough to trust a fringe pattern or a peak Kd. The refined declaration (20 m, the builder's own floor) is what gets delivered. The peak-frame still paints WAVE HEIGHT, which this run publishes no raster of, so its legend is read off the frames alone rather than shared with a panel.
